passage:
Monday. Suraj was helping Pradeep with quadratic equations. "Just do the D thing, then plug into the formula, easy." He raced through three lines, using phrases like "the D thing" and "the usual trick". Pradeep nodded and said "Got it" at every step.

Wednesday. In the class quiz, Pradeep stared at the first question and left half the paper empty. Afterwards he showed Suraj the blank sheet. "I said got it. I didn't."

Saturday. Suraj tried again. What was D? What did a, b and c stand for? He solved one equation slowly and wrote down every step, then handed Pradeep the pen. Pradeep solved the next one with a single mistake, and they fixed it together.

qa.q: What did Pradeep say at every step on Monday?
qa.a: Pradeep said "Got it" at every step.

qa.q: What might Suraj have felt when Pradeep showed the blank quiz sheet?
qa.a: Surprised and guilty, realising the nodding had hidden the confusion.

qa.q: What changed in Suraj's second explanation?
qa.a: Suraj explained what D, a, b and c stood for, solved one equation slowly with every step written down, and handed Pradeep the pen.

qa.q: Why might Pradeep have kept nodding and saying "Got it"?
qa.a: Pradeep probably did not want to seem slow or hold Suraj up, so nodding felt easier than admitting confusion. 🙂

grounding: Shows a teenager skipping steps and using class shorthand while the friend nods without understanding.

passage: Vasudha, sit. I heard you got cross with your friend today, so let me tell you something about me. I'm Divyansh, your uncle, and at sixteen I was the circuit expert in class. Meera asked me to explain Ohm's law. I said, "V equals I R, just rearrange it, the usual, you know," and scribbled symbols fast. She nodded, and I felt clever. Next day she showed me her notebook: three wrong answers and question marks all over. "I nodded because everyone else gets it," she said quietly. I had skipped every step that felt obvious to me. So I took a torch battery, a bulb and a wire, and let her change one thing at a time. That afternoon she finally said, "Oh!"

qa.q: What did Divyansh say when explaining Ohm's law?
qa.a: Divyansh said, "V equals I R, just rearrange it, the usual, you know."

qa.q: How did Divyansh feel after Meera nodded?
qa.a: Clever and satisfied, thinking the explanation had worked.

qa.q: What turning point changed how Divyansh explained?
qa.a: After seeing the question marks in the notebook, Divyansh used a battery, a bulb and a wire so Meera could change one thing at a time.

qa.q: Why did Meera nod even though she did not understand?
qa.a: Meera thought everyone else understood and did not want to be the only one who did not.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling how he skipped obvious steps with shorthand and a nodding friend did not understand.
